title: Bounded contexts
situation: Record corrections, 2026-10-13: an independent architect read the design record cold and found settled decisions contradicting the current design, terms used but never defined, and concepts that disagree; the operator asked for the corrections to be applied. 0003 lists three contexts where there are five, and says a cut lies within one context where the cut concept allows one cut across contexts held by the same architect.
decision: Every concept belongs to exactly one bounded context. Cratylus's contexts are workflow, agents, corpus and delivery, which make the product, and development, which is how the product is made. A cut spans contexts only where the same architect holds them and the whole stays one reviewable change; otherwise one cut per context, joined by contracts. One architect may hold several contexts, but never merges their models. The workflow never models a user's contexts; users bring their own.
consequences: The record now states this as the standing rule.
